schema_comparison.root_cause_of_the_grant_divergence: Supabase PROJECT-CREATION default privileges, which granted anon/authenticated/service_role full rights on every object created in public before 20260805213000 ran `alter default privileges in schema public revoke all on tables from anon, authenticated`. The current Supabase CLI image does not set those defaults, so a fresh replay never receives them. This is the same class of drift 20260806100000_explicit_client_grants.sql and 20260806101000_service_role_grants.sql were written to close for the authenticated-table and service_role-table halves; the anon-table and all-routine halves were never written down. Production's pg_default_acl still shows public/postgres functions as `postgres=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres`, which is why every function carries service_role EXECUTE there and only the 11 explicitly granted ones do in CI.

disposition_of_all_167.principle: 'Platform default ACL' is an origin claim and 'harmless' is a security claim. Each of the 167 is given both, with the query result that establishes it. None is dismissed on the grounds of where it came from.

buckets.origin: platform default ACL - pg_default_acl for public/postgres functions is still `postgres=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres`, never revoked, so every function created gets service_role EXECUTE automatically
buckets.security_consequence: NONE. service_role has rolbypassrls=true and already holds all 544 public table grants - identical and hash-identical on both sides - so EXECUTE on 91 further functions adds nothing it cannot already do directly. Reachable only with the secret service key, never the anon key.
buckets.classification: platform default ACL drift, no security consequence

buckets.what: 52 table DML verbs to anon on 13 tables, 18 to authenticated across 11
buckets.origin: platform default ACL - the stored ACL reads anon=arwdDxtm/postgres, the full 8-privilege default set with grantor postgres, which no hand-authored grant in this repo would ever produce. 20260805213000 revoked the default going forward but `alter default privileges` does not reach objects already created.
buckets.security_consequence: REACHABLE BUT CONTAINED BY RLS. All 55 public base tables have relrowsecurity=true (count without RLS: zero). On each of the 13 anon-reachable tables, the number of policies whose roles include anon or PUBLIC is zero, checked per table. anon and authenticated both have rolbypassrls=false and rolcanlogin=false. A wider GRANT therefore cannot return a row no policy admits.
buckets.classification: platform default ACL drift, security-relevant in principle, contained in fact

buckets.what: routine EXECUTE to anon on 5 functions, to authenticated on 1
buckets.origin: APP-OWNED and never written down - this half was not covered by 20260806100000_explicit_client_grants.sql or 20260806101000_service_role_grants.sql
buckets.security_consequence: CONTAINED. All six functions have prosecdef=false in production - apply_outfit_reaction, claim_command, current_ai_consent_version, log_outfit_wear, plan_outfit_tx - so they are SECURITY INVOKER, execute with the caller's own privileges, and collapse back into the RLS-gated case above. No drift grant lands on a SECURITY DEFINER function.

disposition_of_all_167.the_check_that_would_have_changed_the_ve: anon EXECUTE on a SECURITY DEFINER function would defeat the RLS containment, so it was measured rather than assumed. Production holds 75 SECURITY DEFINER functions of 102, and exactly two are anon-executable: invite_card and join_waitlist. Both are granted by committed migrations, both appear in the replay's grant_routine section, and the replay has exactly two anon rows and no others - so both are intentional and neither is drift. Zero of the 167 confers RLS-bypassing capability.
disposition_of_all_167.honest_severity: REAL, CONTAINED, AND OWED A MIGRATION. Not 'harmless' and not 'exposure'. The access matrix live in production is wider than the one this repo describes, in 167 places, and that gap is unwritten-down by definition. What the evidence rules out is the failure mode that would make it urgent.
disposition_of_all_167.one_difference_runs_the_other_way: log_outfit_wear is executable by authenticated in production and has NO grant to any role in a database built from this repo, so a fresh environment would refuse that RPC. It is superseded by wear_outfit_tx and retained only for old clients, which is why nothing observably breaks - but a rebuilt-from-repo environment is not behaviourally identical to production.
